title: Factor multiplication run
statement: Let $C,e,B$ be natural numbers, let $m$ and $o$ be Boolean flags, let $f$ map finite Boolean words to finite Boolean words, and let $h$ be a finite Boolean word. Suppose $v$ assigns a natural number to each of fourteen registers, every register value is at most $B$, register $11$ is zero, and $Fv_7\le B$, where $F=C$ if $o$ is false and $F=2C+3$ if $o$ is true. Starting in the factor-copy state with flag $o$ and no result, the computation reaches the length-bound state if $o$ is false and the tail-test state with flag true if $o$ is true, with register $7$ equal to $Fv_7$ and every other register unchanged. Every configuration before the final one satisfies the prescribed invariant: the instruction is admissible at that configuration and all register values are at most $B$.

replaced:
Let $C,e,B$ be natural numbers, let the mode and outer flag be Boolean, let $f$ be a
function on bit strings, let $h$ be a bit string, and let $v$ be a fourteen-register
assignment whose values are all at most $B$. If register $11$ is zero and multiplying
register $7$ by the factor $C$ when the outer flag is false, or by $2C+3$ when it is
true, yields a value at most $B$, then the machine reaches the length-bound state when
the outer flag is false and the tail-test state when it is true. It starts in the
factor-copy state with its first flag and no answer recorded, and finishes with register
$7$ replaced by that product and all other registers unchanged, satisfying the
prescribed configuration invariant throughout.
